chunks: And whatever is narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani, I have narrated it from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar Al-Hamadani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ زِيَادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْه: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar Al-Hamadani, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific used for narrators
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, a respected narrator and father of Ibrahim ibn Hashim
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ الْكُرْمَانِيُ: Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani, a prominent Shia narrator

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani verified in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs this biographical note to authenticate the isnad of Muhammad ibn Al-Walid Al-Kirmani, a key narrator in the Kufan school, by tracing the chain through Ahmad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim. This cross-referencing highlights the rigorous methodology of hadith scholars in verifying the reliability of transmitters during the formative period of Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the importance of direct personal receipt (sama') in establishing the credibility of the transmitted text.
